thread:
olivia: Hi team, Olivia here  started today on runtime. Trying to build from source on Ubuntu 22.04 and running into a linker/nvcc mess at the end of the build. Anyone seen this?

olivia: End of link log:```
[ 87%] Linking CXX executable bin/runtime_server
/usr/bin/ld: /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart_static.a(libcudart_static.a.o): relocation R_X86_64_PC32 against symbol `__cudaRegisterLinkedBinary' can not be used when making a shared object; recompile with -fPIC
collect2: error: ld returned 1 exit status
```

paige: welcome! :tada: that libcudart_static complaint usually means a static cuda lib was compiled without -fPIC and you're pulling it into a shared target. Did you install CUDA via apt or the NVIDIA runfile?

olivia: I used the runfile for 12.1 (followed the post-install steps) and symlinked /usr/local/cuda -> /usr/local/cuda-12.1. Also set gcc/g++ alternatives to 11.

sam: two quick checks: 1) try a clean without ccache (we've seen stale objects cause weird relocations), 2) confirm whether the build picks static or shared cudart. If it's dev, building static-only is sometimes faster to iterate: `-DBUILD_SHARED_LIBS=OFF`.

olivia: turned off ccache (ccache -C) and re-ran. Now nvcc bails earlier with ptxas:```
ptxas fatal : Unsupported gpu architecture 'compute_86'
error: command '/usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas' failed with exit status 255
```

paige: that suggests the ptxas on PATH doesn't support sm_86. What's `which ptxas` and `ptxas --version`?

olivia: `which ptxas` -> /usr/local/cuda/bin/ptxas ; `ptxas --version` prints CUDA 11.4. But /usr/local/cuda is a symlink to cuda-12.1, so I'm confused.

sam: likely you have an old CUDA install still in place and /usr/local/cuda/bin is pointing to the newer one but your shell PATH earlier had the old one first (or you have the old binaries lingering in /usr/local/bin). Also check `/usr/bin/which -a ptxas` to see all matches.

olivia: ah yep `which -a ptxas` shows `/usr/local/cuda-11.4/bin/ptxas` before the symlink. I must have edited PATH previously. Reordered PATH so /usr/local/cuda-12.1/bin is first and removed the old entries.

paige: nice. After that you should see `ptxas --version` report 12.x. Also verify `nvcc --version` and `ldd /usr/local/cuda/lib64/libcudart.so` for runtime link targets.

olivia: after fixing PATH and clearing ccache, build progressed further. Final link succeeded but there was a warning about a third-party static lib missing PIC. For day-1 that's fine, but worth documenting in onboarding.

sam: agreed. Action items: add a quick onboarding checklist item to validate CUDA toolchain consistency: `which ptxas`, `ptxas --version`, `nvcc --version`, check ccache state. Also recommend using the devcontainer image we maintain to avoid local toolchain drift.

olivia: happy to open a PR to add that checklist and a tiny shell script that fails early if versions mismatch.

infra-bot: scheduled devcontainer build for tag `devcontainer/cuda-12.1` (request from @olivia) 310 will post artifact link when ready.

buildkite: Build queued: https://buildkite.com/redwood/runtime-devcontainers/builds/4599 (infra)

paige: thanks for the report and the willingness to PR this. Also small tip: if you need to iterate quickly, our CI has a small image you can pull that matches infra's toolchain: `docker pull registry.internal/redwood/runtime-dev:cuda-12.1-dev`. Saves a lot of local tweaking.

olivia: awesome, grabbing that now. Thanks everyone for the quick help! :heart:
